title: Unitary Foundation Releases 2026 Quantum Open Source Survey Covering SDK Adoption, Hybrid HPC Workflows, and AI Tooling - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Unitary Foundation's fifth annual Quantum Open Source Survey (1,800+ respondents) shows Qiskit still dominant but sliding (69.1% to 56.8%) while PennyLane and Classiq gain, IBM leading cloud access, hybrid workflows now mainstream (52.9%), and Claude Code the top AI coding assistant (71.6%) among quantum developers who verify AI outputs heavily.

themes.theme: SDK and cloud platform share shifts

insights.claim: In the 2026 Unitary Foundation Quantum Open Source Survey, Qiskit remained the leading full-stack SDK at 56.8% active usage but fell from 69.1% in 2025, while PennyLane rose from 30.8% to 34.3%.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM's software moat is eroding at the margin; Xanadu's PennyLane is the gaining challenger.

insights.claim: Classiq shows strong momentum among quantum developers: Classiq Library has 21.4% SDK usage with 23.4% planning to adopt it next year, Classiq holds 22.8% of quantum cloud service usage (second to IBM) with 25.7% next-year intent, and Classiq Library ties for the top applications tool at 23.2%.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Classiq is emerging as a platform-agnostic software layer with broad mindshare; relevant to private valuation and partnership watch.

insights.claim: IBM Quantum Platform leads quantum cloud access at 54.9% active usage and 33.4% next-year intent, ahead of Classiq (22.8%), Amazon Braket (17.9%), qBraid (17.0%) and Azure Quantum (9.6%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler quantum clouds (AWS, Microsoft) trail IBM materially in developer usage.

insights.claim: Classiq Library (24.9%) and NVIDIA CUDA-Q Algorithms (21.2%) recorded the highest planned adoption rates among quantum application tools for 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's software ecosystem is penetrating quantum application development, reinforcing its role as the classical side of hybrid quantum.

insights.claim: 35.2% of surveyed quantum practitioners use QEC tools, led by Qiskit (51.7%), PennyLane (30.0%), Stim (29.8%), NVIDIA CUDA-Q QEC (20.8%), PyMatching (15.8%) and Riverlane Deltakit (13.5%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: QEC tooling is a nascent but real market segment where NVIDIA and Riverlane are gaining footholds.

insights.claim: Among non-users of QEC tools (n = 1,043), 22.8% cite cost and 19.0% cite missing tool implementations as barriers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Missing implementations suggest whitespace for QEC software vendors.

insights.claim: Quantum error correction ranks as the second research priority (44.4%) behind algorithm development (54.3%) and ahead of application development (42.6%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Practitioner focus is shifting toward fault tolerance, aligning with vendor logical-qubit roadmaps.

themes.theme: AI coding assistants in quantum development

insights.claim: Among quantum developers using AI coding assistants, Anthropic Claude Code leads at 71.6% usage, followed by OpenAI Codex (41.8%), Google Gemini (39.4%), Microsoft Copilot (16.6%) and Cursor (11.3%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A niche but technically demanding developer cohort strongly prefers Anthropic's coding agent, a datapoint on AI coding tool competition.

insights.claim: 77.8% of surveyed quantum practitioners use AI tools for quantum workflows, mainly for debugging/optimization (77.0%) and learning SDKs (76.4%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AI assistants are lowering the onboarding cost for quantum SDKs, which may accelerate developer base growth.

insights.claim: Quantum practitioners rate AI productivity gains at 3.1 out of 4.0 but have lower confidence in AI code accuracy (2.5) and conceptual explanations (2.6), so 42.9% always and 38.7% mostly verify AI outputs, chiefly via manual review (78.3%) and automated tests (54.2%) rather than formal verification (17.5%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Trust gap in AI-generated quantum code creates demand for verification and testing tooling.

insights.claim: 52.9% of surveyed quantum practitioners ran hybrid quantum-classical workflows in the past year, using CPU simulators (80.2%), GPU-accelerated simulators (56.4%), QPU execution with classical pre/post-processing (46.8%), iterative loops (36.7%) and real-time feedback pipelines (21.3%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid is now the majority workflow, supporting GPU and HPC vendors' quantum strategies.

insights.claim: Among the 36.8% of quantum practitioners using HPC tools, NVIDIA CUDA (24.1%) and Slurm (17.0%) are most common, while top scaling bottlenecks are limited QPU access (54.4%), compute cost (41.8%), constrained GPU/HPC availability (37.0%) and quantum-classical integration friction (25.4%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: QPU access scarcity is the top constraint, implying latent demand for on-prem and cloud QPU capacity.

insights.claim: Quantum survey respondents are mostly researchers (49.4%) and software developers (34.2%); 46.6% work in quantum as a primary paid job and 56.2% have two or fewer years of professional quantum experience.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A young, fast-growing workforce; talent depth remains thin.

insights.claim: Participation in the 2026 quantum open source survey was led by the United States (17.7%), India (15.7%), Israel (15.5%), Canada (7.7%), the United Kingdom (5.1%) and Germany (5.0%).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Israel's outsized share is notable relative to its size (possibly tied to Classiq's base).

insights.claim: Python dominates quantum development at 92.5%, C/C++ rose from 27.8% in 2025 to 33.9% in 2026, and Rust (14.0% active) ranks first at 45.3% among languages respondents plan to learn.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shift toward performance languages reflects real-time control and decoding needs as hardware matures.
